newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up 13 pct in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up 13 pct in heavy trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed up 13.26 percent in heavy trading on Monday due to continuing rumours that Beijing was drafting measures to boost the market, brokers said.
The B index surged 15.62 points to 133.44 after hitting an intra-session high of 134.26, with turnover expanding to HK$347.13 million from HK$147.07 million on Friday.

"The gap between the prices of B shares and their A counterparts is fueling buying interest in class B equity," one broker said. "But the rise was a little too quick and steep and the potential for profit-taking is increasing," she said.
One analyst said institutions are enlarging their holdings due to China's improving economy.
"Monday's healthy turnover indicated investor optimism over the market's short-term outlook," a second analyst said.
Television maker Huafa, the sharpest gainer, surged HK$0.72, or 27.38 percent, to HK$3.35 on volume of 353,800 shares due to speculative buying, brokers said.
Chiwan Wharf rose HK$1.10, or 22.54 percent, to HK$5.98 on trade of 944,300 shares. The firm said on Friday it expected its newly completed bulk cargo and grain warehouse to boost profits in 1997.
Changan Automobile put on HK$0.54 to HK$3.23 on the session's most active trade of 17.55 million shares.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times quoted a Changan spokesman as saying the firm posted 1.96 billion yuan in sales in the first ten months of this year and is likely to surpass its 1996 net profits target.
Motorcycle producer North Jianshe jumped HK$0.57 to HK$3.37 and refrigerator maker Meilin firmed HK$0.54 to HK$4.54 because of institutional demand, brokers said.

The A market rose on heavy speculative demand, brokers said. The A index advanced 12.35 points, or 2.77 percent, to close at its intraday high of 457.44 on turnover of 16.39 billion yuan, compared with Friday's 11.52 billion. The composite index closed up 13.18 points, or 3.17 percent, at 429.24.
Sichuan Changjiang climbed 1.64 yuan, or 14.94 percent, to 12.62 yuan on volume of 12.19 million shares due to speculative buying, brokers said.
